info.title: OpenAsy Messages API
info.summary: Email, SMS and WhatsApp campaigns and journeys through your own providers, only to people whose consent holds when each message is sent.
info.description:
Every screen of Messages uses this API, and so can your scripts (ADR 0014). Within `/api/v1` changes are additive only; anything removed is deprecated first (ADR 0024). Errors use Problem Details (RFC 9457).

Providers, consent, the linked products and tracking come from the settings file, never the API. Opens, clicks and unsubscribes are at `/o/`, `/c/` and `/u/`, which people reach from a message, and the providers call `/hooks/`. Everything else takes the session of a signed-in person or an API token, and each operation names the role it needs (`x-openasy-role`: viewer, editor, admin; ADR 0003).

Sign-in, members and API tokens are under `/api/v1/auth`, provided by [@openasy/auth](https://github.com/openasy/auth#routes).

200.description: Metrics in the Prometheus text format.

session.name: __Host-openasy-session
session.description: The browser session after signing in (`openasy-session` when Messages runs on plain http://localhost). Requests that change something must come from the Messages origin.

apiToken.description: An API token created under Settings, API tokens (`oa_messages_...`): one role, always an expiry (ADR 0003).

adminToken.description: Only when Messages is started by its tests or a local script: one shared token with the admin role. A production install does not have it.

Problem.description: An error, as RFC 9457 Problem Details.

missing.description: Environment variables the file names for it that are not set.

state.description: working: its last send went; failing: its last call failed; standby: not used yet; waiting: a key is missing.

config.description: messages.yaml as applied, with names of environment variables, never their values.

unknown.description: Messages that may or may not have been sent, which are never sent again.

waiting.description: Why a channel's messages are waiting, by channel: no provider, quiet hours, Consent away.

held.description: Held back because consent did not hold when they were to be sent.

approval.description: Meta's answer for a WhatsApp template: APPROVED, PENDING, REJECTED, PAUSED or DISABLED.

subject.description: Emails only; may use personal fields.

body.description: Text with {{fields}}; for email, text (paragraphs, [words](https://...)) or HTML. For WhatsApp, the approved body with {{1}}, {{2}}.

as.description: Which of the sample people; the first by default.

csv.description: The file's text: a header with email or phone, and name, user_id and any fields.

skipped.description: Rows without an email or a phone.

name.description: Given back; read from Audience or the list.

allowed.description: May get a message now; consent is asked again for each one when it is sent.

otherwise.description: exit, or the id of a later step.
